- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.4) and prices are rising, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day after sentiment drop.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6) and recent price is trending upward; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture breakout potential.
